canonical_goal.target_object: For every evaluated tuple (N,d,λ,T) with N∈{2,3}, d∈{2,3,4}, λ>0, and finite path/loop truncation T, an interval certificate [L_{N,d,T}(λ),U_{N,d,T}(λ)] for the exact normalized plaquette Wilson-loop expectation p_{N,d}(λ)=⟨w(P)⟩, where w(C)=N^{-1}tr(∏_{e∈C}U_e), P is a length-4 plaquette loop, and the expectation is taken with Wilson action S=-(N/(2λ))∑_{P'}tr(U_{P'}+U_{P'}^†). The certificate is obtained by defining F_{N,d,T,λ} as the finite real feasible set of retained moment assignments X_T satisfying w(tr(1))=1, positive-semidefinite Hermitian matrices A^H_{ab}=⟨tr(P_a^†P_b)⟩, positive-semidefinite ordinary-reflection matrices A^R_{ab}=⟨tr(R[P_a]^†P_b)⟩ with R(x,y,z)=(-x,y,z), retained link-variation Schwinger-Dyson equalities, the SU(2) reduction 2w(C_1)w(C_2)=w(C_1C_2)+w(C_1C̄_2) when N=2, and the SU(3) triple-trace reduction w(C_1)w(C_2)w(C_3)=-(1/9)(w(C_1C_2C_3)+w(C_3C_2C_1))+(1/3)(w(C_1)w(C_2C_3)+w(C_2)w(C_3C_1)+w(C_3)w(C_1C_2))+(1/3)w(C̄_1C_2)w(C̄_1C_3)-(1/9)w(C̄_1C_2C̄_1C_3) when N=3; the outcome records L_{N,d,T}(λ)=inf_{X_T∈F_{N,d,T,λ}}x_P(X_T) and U_{N,d,T}(λ)=sup_{X_T∈F_{N,d,T,λ}}x_P(X_T), with the target property L_{N,d,T}(λ)≤p_{N,d}(λ)≤U_{N,d,T}(λ).
feasibility_constraints: The lattice is Γ_d={x: x=a∑_{μ=1}^{d} n_μ μ̂, n_μ∈ℤ}; each oriented edge from x to x+μ̂ carries U_μ(x)∈SU(N), and reversing orientation uses U_μ(x)^†=U_{-μ}(x+μ̂).

The probability weight is defined by the Wilson action S=-(N/(2λ))∑_{P}tr(U_P+U_P^†), partition function Z=∫∏_{x,μ}dU_μ(x) exp((N/(2λ))∑_{P}tr(U_P+U_P^†)), and expectation ⟨O⟩=Z^{-1}∫∏_{x,μ}dU_μ(x) exp((N/(2λ))∑_{P}tr(U_P+U_P^†))O.

For every finite truncation T, X_T assigns real values to all retained Wilson-loop moment variables needed for the chosen path operators, including single-trace variables w(C) and, for SU(3), retained double-trace variables w_x(C_1)w_y(C_2); the identity loop is fixed by w(tr(1))=1.

Hermitian positivity is imposed as A^H_T⪰0 for each retained set of open paths {P_a} sharing endpoints, with entries A^H_{ab}=⟨tr(P_a^†P_b)⟩; equivalently, for every real vector c, ∑_{a,b}c_ac_b⟨tr(P_a^†P_b)⟩≥0.

Reflection positivity is imposed as A^R_T⪰0 for each retained mirror-reflection path set, with entries A^R_{ab}=⟨tr(Θ[P_a]P_b)⟩, where the reflection R maps (x,y,z) to (-x,y,z) across the plane x=0 and Θ[P]=R[P]^†; equivalently, for every real vector c, ∑_{a,b}c_ac_b⟨tr(Θ[P_a]P_b)⟩≥0.

For retained single-trace loops C, the normalized link-variation equality is imposed: ∑_{±ν≠μ}(⟨w(μνμ̄ν̄C)⟩-⟨w(νμν̄μ̄C)⟩) -(2λ/N^2)(ň_+-n_-)⟨w(C)⟩ +2λ[∑_{j_+=1}^{ň_+}⟨w_x(C_{x,x+})w_x(C_{x+,x})⟩-∑_{j_-=1}^{n_-}⟨w_x(C_{x,x-})w_x(C_{x-,x})⟩] -∑_{±ν≠μ}(⟨w_x(μνμ̄ν̄)w_x(C)⟩-⟨w_x(νμν̄μ̄)w_x(C)⟩)=0, where ň_+ counts all edges in C at the same position and direction as μ, including μ itself, and n_- counts all edges in C at the same position and opposite direction as μ.

For SU(2), every double trace is reduced by 2w(C_1)w(C_2)=w(C_1C_2)+w(C_1C̄_2). For SU(3), double-trace variables are retained, and every generated triple trace is eliminated by w(C_1)w(C_2)w(C_3)=-(1/9)(w(C_1C_2C_3)+w(C_3C_2C_1))+(1/3)(w(C_1)w(C_2C_3)+w(C_2)w(C_3C_1)+w(C_3)w(C_1C_2))+(1/3)w(C̄_1C_2)w(C̄_1C_3)-(1/9)w(C̄_1C_2C̄_1C_3), so a feasible SU(3) truncation contains no independent triple-trace variables.

The reported lower bound is the infimum of the plaquette variable over all X_T satisfying the retained positive-semidefinite and equality constraints, and the reported upper bound is the supremum of the same plaquette variable over the same feasible set.

canonical_goal.target_object: An exact two-dimensional twist-reflection positivity statement: for paths P_a whose endpoints are at the origin and whose links lie on the chosen side of the two-dimensional lattice, define R_t(x,y)=(-x,-y), define Θ_t[P]=R_t[P]^†, and define A^t_{ab}=⟨tr(Θ_t[P_a]P_b)⟩; the target proposition is A^t⪰0, equivalently ∑_{a,b}c_ac_b⟨tr(Θ_t[P_a]P_b)⟩≥0 for every real coefficient vector c.
feasibility_constraints: The lattice dimension is d=2, with Wilson action S=-(N/(2λ))∑_P tr(U_P+U_P^†), λ>0, and compact link variables U_μ(x)∈SU(N).

The twist reflection maps the positive side of the lattice to the negative side by (x,y)↦(-x,-y), maps the two half-lines U_{0+} and U_{0-} into each other, and is combined with Hermitian conjugation by Θ_t[P]=R_t[P]^†.

The proof is allowed to impose a gauge on the one-dimensional separating line in two dimensions such that U_{0+}=U_{0-}=1, so the path-integral factor containing P and Θ_t[P] factorizes as |∫DU_+ exp(-S_{U_+})P(U_+)|^2, which is nonnegative.
The path set used to form A^t is finite, and every matrix entry A^t_{ab} is a gauge-invariant Wilson loop formed by sewing Θ_t[P_a] to P_b.

success_set.definition: Σ_2={o_2: for every finite path set {P_a} with endpoints (0,0) and links contained in U_+∪U_{0+}, where U_+={(x,y):x>0} and U_{0+}={(0,y):y>0}, the matrix A^t with entries A^t_{ab}=⟨tr(Θ_t[P_a]P_b)⟩ is positive semidefinite; equivalently, for every real vector c and P_c=∑_a c_aP_a, the scalar ∑_{a,b}c_ac_b⟨tr(Θ_t[P_a]P_b)⟩ equals a squared-modulus two-dimensional path-integral expression after a gauge sets all link variables on the separating one-dimensional line {(0,y):y∈aℤ} to the identity matrix, and therefore the scalar is ≥0}.

preference_ordering.definition: A twist-reflection statement o is weakly preferred to o′ when o proves positive semidefiniteness for every finite path set covered by o′ and additionally covers at least one finite path set not covered by o′; statements that require assumptions false in d=2 are not feasible and are not comparable to feasible statements.

canonical_goal.target_object: A closed SU(3) Wilson-loop bootstrap constraint system whose variables are single-trace moments w(C)=3^{-1}tr(∏_{e∈C}U_e) and double-trace moments w_x(C_1)w_y(C_2), where x and y record the starting positions of the two loops. The target proposition is that every retained single-trace link-variation equality and every retained double-trace link-variation equality can be written using only those single- and double-trace variables after eliminating each generated triple trace by the SU(3) identity w(C_1)w(C_2)w(C_3)=-(1/9)(w(C_1C_2C_3)+w(C_3C_2C_1))+(1/3)(w(C_1)w(C_2C_3)+w(C_2)w(C_3C_1)+w(C_3)w(C_1C_2))+(1/3)w(C̄_1C_2)w(C̄_1C_3)-(1/9)w(C̄_1C_2C̄_1C_3); no independent variable of the form w(C_1)w(C_2)w(C_3) remains in the finite optimization problem.
feasibility_constraints: The gauge group is SU(3), the normalized Wilson loop is w(C)=3^{-1}tr(∏_{e∈C}U_e), and double-trace variables have the form w_x(C_1)w_y(C_2), where x and y record the starting positions of the two loops.

For a single-trace loop C varied at a link μ, the SU(3) single-trace equality is ∑_{±ν≠μ}(⟨w(μνμ̄ν̄C)⟩-⟨w(νμν̄μ̄C)⟩) -(2λ/9)(ň_+-n_-)⟨w(C)⟩ +2λ[∑_{j_+=1}^{ň_+}⟨w_x(C_{x,x+})w_x(C_{x+,x})⟩-∑_{j_-=1}^{n_-}⟨w_x(C_{x,x-})w_x(C_{x-,x})⟩] -∑_{±ν≠μ}(⟨w_x(μνμ̄ν̄)w_x(C)⟩-⟨w_x(νμν̄μ̄)w_x(C)⟩)=0, where ň_+ counts all edges in C at the same position and direction as μ, including μ itself, and n_- counts all edges in C at the same position and opposite direction as μ.

For a double-trace variable w_x(C_1)w_y(C_2), variation of a link μ in C_1 imposes an equality containing: plaquette-insertion terms on C_1 multiplied by w_y(C_2); a coefficient -(2λ/9)(ň_{1,+}-n_{1,-}+n_{2,+}-n_{2,-}) multiplying ⟨w_x(C_1)w_y(C_2)⟩; sewing terms (2λ/9)[∑_{j_+=1}^{n_{2,+}}⟨w(C_{1,x}C_{2,x+})⟩-∑_{j_-=1}^{n_{2,-}}⟨w(C_{1,x}C_{2,x-})⟩]; split-loop triple-trace terms 2λ[∑_{j_+=1}^{ň_{1,+}}⟨w_x(C_{1,x,x+})w_x(C_{1,x+,x})w_y(C_2)⟩-∑_{j_-=1}^{n_{1,-}}⟨w_x(C_{1,x,x-})w_x(C_{1,x-,x})w_y(C_2)⟩]; and plaquette-loop subtraction terms -∑_{±ν≠μ}(⟨w_x(μνμ̄ν̄)w_x(C_1)w_y(C_2)⟩-⟨w_x(νμν̄μ̄)w_x(C_1)w_y(C_2)⟩)=0.

Every triple trace generated in the retained equations is reduced by w(C_1)w(C_2)w(C_3)=-(1/9)(w(C_1C_2C_3)+w(C_3C_2C_1))+(1/3)(w(C_1)w(C_2C_3)+w(C_2)w(C_3C_1)+w(C_3)w(C_1C_2))+(1/3)w(C̄_1C_2)w(C̄_1C_3)-(1/9)w(C̄_1C_2C̄_1C_3).

success_set.definition: Σ_3={o_3: every retained SU(3) single-trace and double-trace link variation is represented as a finite equality among retained single-trace and double-trace moment variables after applying the triple-trace reduction identity w(C_1)w(C_2)w(C_3)=-(1/9)(w(C_1C_2C_3)+w(C_3C_2C_1))+(1/3)(w(C_1)w(C_2C_3)+w(C_2)w(C_3C_1)+w(C_3)w(C_1C_2))+(1/3)w(C̄_1C_2)w(C̄_1C_3)-(1/9)w(C̄_1C_2C̄_1C_3), and no independent triple-trace optimization variable remains in the final finite bootstrap system}.

methodological_claim.target_object: A finite positivity-bootstrap workflow and path-selection methodology for SU(3) lattice Yang-Mills plaquette bounds. Given a finite path system T, the workflow creates variables X_T for sewn Wilson loops and required double-trace products, imposes positive-semidefinite Hermitian matrices A^H_{ab}=⟨tr(P_a^†P_b)⟩, imposes positive-semidefinite ordinary-reflection matrices A^R_{ab}=⟨tr(R[P_a]^†P_b)⟩, imposes positive-semidefinite twist-reflection matrices A^t_{ab}=⟨tr(Θ_t[P_a]P_b)⟩ only in exactly two-dimensional constructions where R_t(x,y)=(-x,-y) and the separating one-dimensional line can be gauged to the identity, imposes retained link-variation equalities, eliminates SU(3) triple traces by w(C_1)w(C_2)w(C_3)=-(1/9)(w(C_1C_2C_3)+w(C_3C_2C_1))+(1/3)(w(C_1)w(C_2C_3)+w(C_2)w(C_3C_1)+w(C_3)w(C_1C_2))+(1/3)w(C̄_1C_2)w(C̄_1C_3)-(1/9)w(C̄_1C_2C̄_1C_3), and returns the plaquette interval [inf_{X_T∈F_T}x_P(X_T), sup_{X_T∈F_T}x_P(X_T)]. The path-selection component restricts 2D paths to ladder-type loops contained in {(x,y):x∈aℤ, y∈{0,a}} and restricts 3D or 4D paths to plane-type paths contained in a chosen (d-1)-dimensional coordinate subplane, thereby reducing the number of retained loop variables while still producing finite SDP bounds for the plaquette variable.

evidence_channels.formalisation: Let T be a finite selected path system and x_P the retained plaquette variable. Define F_T as the set of assignments X_T satisfying: A^H_T⪰0 for matrices A^H_{ab}=⟨tr(P_a^†P_b)⟩; A^R_T⪰0 for matrices A^R_{ab}=⟨tr(R[P_a]^†P_b)⟩; A^t_T⪰0 exactly for two-dimensional twist-reflection path sets with R_t(x,y)=(-x,-y), Θ_t[P]=R_t[P]^†, endpoints at (0,0), and links in U_+∪U_{0+}; E_T(X_T)=0 for retained link-variation equations; R_T(X_T)=0 for SU(3) reductions generated by w(C_1)w(C_2)w(C_3)=-(1/9)(w(C_1C_2C_3)+w(C_3C_2C_1))+(1/3)(w(C_1)w(C_2C_3)+w(C_2)w(C_3C_1)+w(C_3)w(C_1C_2))+(1/3)w(C̄_1C_2)w(C̄_1C_3)-(1/9)w(C̄_1C_2C̄_1C_3); and w(tr(1))=1. The workflow output is (inf_{X_T∈F_T}x_P(X_T), sup_{X_T∈F_T}x_P(X_T)). The dimensional path-selection rule replaces the unrestricted set of paths of bounded length by ladder-type paths in {(x,y):x∈aℤ, y∈{0,a}} for d=2 and by plane-type paths in a chosen (d-1)-dimensional coordinate subplane for d∈{3,4}.

stated_goal.formalisation: The stated goal is the instrumental conjunction of four formal targets: (i) construct certified intervals [L_{N,d,T}(λ),U_{N,d,T}(λ)] for p_{N,d}(λ)=⟨N^{-1}tr(U_P)⟩ under S=-(N/(2λ))∑_{P'}tr(U_{P'}+U_{P'}^†), primarily for N=3 and d∈{2,3,4}; (ii) prove exact positive semidefiniteness of A^t_{ab}=⟨tr(Θ_t[P_a]P_b)⟩ in d=2 for R_t(x,y)=(-x,-y); (iii) close SU(3) multi-trace loop equations by retaining double traces and reducing triple traces through w(C_1)w(C_2)w(C_3)=-(1/9)(w(C_1C_2C_3)+w(C_3C_2C_1))+(1/3)(w(C_1)w(C_2C_3)+w(C_2)w(C_3C_1)+w(C_3)w(C_1C_2))+(1/3)w(C̄_1C_2)w(C̄_1C_3)-(1/9)w(C̄_1C_2C̄_1C_3); and (iv) use ladder-type paths in a one-plaquette-thick strip for d=2 and plane-type paths in a chosen (d-1)-dimensional coordinate subplane for d∈{3,4} to reduce finite SDP size.

operational_goal.formalisation: For each reported finite path/loop truncation T and coupling λ, the operational problem is to minimize and maximize x_P(X_T) over retained Wilson-loop moment variables X_T subject to w(tr(1))=1, positive-semidefinite Hermitian matrices A^H_{ab}=⟨tr(P_a^†P_b)⟩, positive-semidefinite ordinary-reflection matrices A^R_{ab}=⟨tr(R[P_a]^†P_b)⟩, positive-semidefinite twist-reflection matrices A^t_{ab}=⟨tr(Θ_t[P_a]P_b)⟩ exactly for the two-dimensional twist-reflection constructions with R_t(x,y)=(-x,-y), retained link-variation equalities, and SU(3) reductions of triple traces by w(C_1)w(C_2)w(C_3)=-(1/9)(w(C_1C_2C_3)+w(C_3C_2C_1))+(1/3)(w(C_1)w(C_2C_3)+w(C_2)w(C_3C_1)+w(C_3)w(C_1C_2))+(1/3)w(C̄_1C_2)w(C̄_1C_3)-(1/9)w(C̄_1C_2C̄_1C_3). The reported convergence object is the interval [inf_{X_T}x_P(X_T), sup_{X_T}x_P(X_T)] as T is enlarged.

inference_basis: The abstract names rigorous plaquette bounds, convergence, consistency with known reference results, twist-reflection positivity, dimensional-reduction truncation, and double-trace Schwinger-Dyson equations as the paper's main achievements.
Section 2.2 defines the optimization object: positive-semidefinite constraints plus loop-equation equalities produce upper and lower bounds on Wilson-loop expectation values.

Sections 6 and 7 repeatedly instantiate the same optimization target for 2D, 3D, and 4D SU(2)/SU(3) plaquette expectations, while Section 8 states that the 3D and 4D aim is proof of principle rather than optimality.

The introduction and discussion frame higher-rank applicability and hadronic-physics relevance as motivation, but the operational artifacts are finite SDP plaquette-bound certificates and exact/derived constraints.
implicit_goal.formalisation: The best-fitting implicit goal is an instrumental conjunction with outcome o=( [L_{N,d,T}(λ),U_{N,d,T}(λ)]_{N,d,λ,T}, A^t, E^{(1)}_{SU(3)}, E^{(2)}_{SU(3)}, R^{(3→≤2)}_{SU(3)} ). The first component is preferred when L_{N,d,T}(λ)≤⟨N^{-1}tr(U_P)⟩≤U_{N,d,T}(λ) and the total width ∑_{N,d,λ,T}(U_{N,d,T}(λ)-L_{N,d,T}(λ)) is smaller. The second component is successful when A^t_{ab}=⟨tr(R_t[P_a]^†P_b)⟩ is positive semidefinite in d=2 for R_t(x,y)=(-x,-y). The third, fourth, and fifth components are successful when every retained SU(3) single- and double-trace link-variation equation is expressed using at most two trace factors after applying w(C_1)w(C_2)w(C_3)=-(1/9)(w(C_1C_2C_3)+w(C_3C_2C_1))+(1/3)(w(C_1)w(C_2C_3)+w(C_2)w(C_3C_1)+w(C_3)w(C_1C_2))+(1/3)w(C̄_1C_2)w(C̄_1C_3)-(1/9)w(C̄_1C_2C̄_1C_3).

paper_goal.consistency_relation_derivation: The stated and operational channels align on the formal target of certified plaquette bounds and on the auxiliary formal targets of exact two-dimensional twist-reflection positivity and SU(3) multi-trace closure. However, the stated channel also includes motivational and forward-looking framing about QCD, hadronic physics, and broad non-perturbative investigations; those claims are not themselves optimized, proved, or evaluated by the finite SDP constructions. Therefore the extraction uses framing_divergence rather than aligned.
